faq: Will a popup hurt my search ranking?
Not if it follows Google's guidance. We avoid full-screen popups on mobile that block the content straight away, and we use delays so visitors can see your page first.
Can I offer a discount for signing up?
Yes, but it is not required. We can offer a guide, early access or entry to a drawing where legal. We set the offer you choose and match the form copy to it.
We add clear wording and a checkbox where your region needs it, and we link to your privacy policy. Text opt-ins always get separate, explicit consent wording.
Will it work with my store theme?
Yes for Shopify, WooCommerce and most site builders. The forms load from your email tool's code or app, and we test them on the live theme without changing your design.

desc:
Email signup forms and popups are how a store turns visitors into subscribers. Ecom Swift LLC designs and installs them in your own tool, with sensible timing, clear consent, source tags and a welcome message ready for each new subscriber.

## What are email signup forms and popups?

Email signup forms and popups are the places on your website where a visitor can give an email address, and sometimes a phone number, to hear from you. A popup appears over the page. An embedded form sits in the page itself, such as in the footer or a blog post. A flyout is a small tab that stays at the edge of the screen.

Each form should ask for as little as possible, say what the person will receive and send the details to the right list.

## Why a polite form is worth the effort

Most visitors do not buy on their first visit. A signup form lets you stay in touch with those who are interested but not ready. Without one, you pay again to bring them back through ads or search.

A badly timed popup, though, annoys people. If it covers the page the second someone arrives, or returns after they have already subscribed, visitors leave. A polite form waits until a visitor has shown interest, offers something worth reading, appears properly on a phone and never blocks checkout. How well it performs depends on your traffic, offer and design, so we build forms that are easy to test and adjust.

## What a good signup setup includes

- A clear headline that says what subscribers get, such as news, early access or a first-order reason.
- A short form, usually just an email address to begin with.
- Triggers based on delay or scroll depth, not an instant pop.
- Separate phone and desktop versions that are easy to close.
- A consent checkbox or statement where rules require it.
- Text opt-in as a second step, with plain wording about frequency and stopping.
- Hiding rules, so the form stays off checkout and away from existing subscribers.
- A source tag for each form, so you know where subscribers come from.
- A thank-you message that gives a next step.
- A test signup that reaches your list and starts the welcome message.

## How we install it

We look at your site, your brand and where your visitors come from. Then we design the forms in your own email or SMS tool, choose the triggers and placement, and make them match your fonts and colors. We submit test signups on a phone and a computer to confirm the contact lands in the right list with the right tag.

The Basic package delivers one popup with timing, phone and desktop versions, a consent checkbox where required and a test signup. Standard adds two embedded forms, a success message with a next step, source tags, hiding rules and a text opt-in step. Premium builds up to four forms including a flyout, a short quiz and an A/B test of two popup offers, followed by a handover call. Add-ons include extra forms, a spin-to-win popup and an exit-intent popup. Forms should not harm how your site loads, so we keep scripts light.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Offer a real reason to subscribe.
- Make the close button easy to see and tap.
- Ask for the minimum details first.
- Say how often you will write.
- Test on a real phone before launch.

**Avoid:**
- Firing a popup the instant a visitor lands on a page.
- Covering the full screen on mobile.
- Pre-ticking consent boxes.
- Appearing again after someone subscribed.
- Running several popups at once.

## Who it suits

A store with traffic but a tiny list will benefit most. A new brand that wants a polite way to collect interest before launch can use an embedded form and a waitlist. A store with an old popup that annoys visitors can replace it with something better timed.

## What we need from you

Share your site address, the email or SMS tool, your brand assets, any offer you want to show and the wording you prefer. We never need passwords. Access is given as a collaborator, staff or team user where the platform supports it, and you remain the owner of every account.
